subject: PayLane: autoscale verification & performance next steps
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@paylane.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@paylane.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jan 2028 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets and burst expectations (PayLane)

Thanks again for the demo today — that was really helpful. A couple of items I want to make sure we captured from the call so our SRE and platform teams can align: 

- Latency targets: p95 generation for our 256-token typical responses should be <= 400ms (end-to-end from request to final chunk). For heavy flows (up to 1024 tokens) p95 budget is 1.2s.
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency target is ~220 concurrent inference connections; peak concurrency during our marketing spikes could reach ~800 for short windows (5–10 minutes).
- Throughput/burst: typical baseline traffic is ~180 req/s; during promotions we need to absorb bursts up to ~2,000 req/s for ~8–12 minutes.
- Streaming: we rely on token-by-token streaming for UX; startup latency to first token must be <200ms for short prompts.
- Scale-up expectations: we need guidance on warm-pool sizes and expected time-to-ready for cold-started workers — ideally <45s to reach steady processing for scaled instances.

Can you confirm the above captures what your team heard, and propose a verification plan (synthetic runs / prewarmed pool sizes / priming policy) we can share with our infra team? I attached a short prompt set to use as a sample.

Thanks,
Elena
Sr. SRE, PayLane

Attachment: paylane_promptset_v1.csv (CSV, 48 rows)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@paylane.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jan 2028 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets and burst expectations (PayLane)

Elena — thanks for the clear summary. That matches what we captured on the call. Quick confirmation + proposed next steps below.

Confirmation (short):
- We can support token streaming and target the first-token <200ms path when requests hit prewarmed serving lanes.
- For your p95 numbers (<=400ms for 256 tokens, <=1.2s for 1024), we'll need to validate with your exact prompt distribution and sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, n).
- Bursts to ~2,000 req/s are achievable with a combination of: prewarmed pool, aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and a queueing allowance for brief overage.

Proposed verification plan (high level):
1) Synthetic baseline run (we run on our staging cluster with your promptset): measure p50/p95/p99 for 256/512/1024 tokens and streaming startup time.
2) Burst soak test: ramp from baseline to 2k req/s over 60s and hold for 12 minutes; observe scale behavior, queuing, and tail latency.
3) Warm-pool sizing exercise: iterate on prewarmed lanes in increments (20 / 40 / 80) to measure first-token and p95 improvements.
4) Failure/fallback test: simulate partial zone capacity loss and validate automatic fallback to cheaper model variants without violating SLOs.

Action items — please:
- Confirm sampling parameters and any prompt-level fallback rules we should honor.
- Grant us access to the promptset link (or confirm the attached CSV is canonical).

I'll kick off a more detailed test plan and timeline after Aditya and Ben weigh in on resource estimates.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@paylane.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jan 2028 18:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets and burst expectations (PayLane)

Looping in the rough test matrix and resource ask so we can align on dates: 

Test matrix (summary):
- Workload profiles: short (<=256 tokens, 60% of traffic), medium (257–512, 30%), long (512–1024, 10%).
- Sampling: top_p=0.95, temp=0.2 (PayLane to confirm).
- Concurrency target steps: 100 / 220 / 400 / 800.
- Burst profile: 180 req/s baseline -> ramp to 2,000 req/s in 60s, hold 12 min, then drop.
- Metrics: first-byte latency, first-token time, p50/p95/p99 generation, CPU/GPU util, queue length, model variant fallback count.

Preliminary resource estimate (staging): 40 prewarmed lanes for baseline; add +60 lanes to sustain 2k req/s depending on batching efficacy and model size. This is a starting point; the warm-pool sizing exercise will refine it.

Deliverables I'll prepare by EOD tomorrow (Tue):
- rdw_autoscale_plan_v2.xlsx (detailed stepper and expected resource curves)
- a short JMeter script and artifact instructions to reproduce the burst locally
- a list of perf hooks we'll add to the test harness to capture queueing events and fallback triggers

Ben — can you review whether 40 prewarmed lanes is a reasonable initial value for PayLane's model (they're using a 7B quantized variant)?

Elena — once you confirm sampling and approve the test window (we suggest Wed 2/1 02:00–06:00 UTC for staging), we'll schedule and reserve capacity.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Perf Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rdw_autoscale_plan_v2.xlsx (Excel, perf matrix)
From: Elena Torres <elena@paylane.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@paylane.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Jan 2028 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets and burst expectations (PayLane)

Thank you — that plan looks good. A few clarifications and confirmations: 

- Sampling confirmed: top_p=0.95, temp=0.2 — we'll send a sanitized subset of the full promptset (production contains PII). The attached CSV is fine for initial runs.
- Test window: Wed 2028-02-01 02:00–06:00 UTC works for us (SRE team will be on-call).
- Prewarmed lanes: Carlos and I are comfortable with the 40 -> +60 ramp as a starting hypothesis; please include cost/seconds estimates in the plan so we can model spend.
- Fallback rules: if model variant fallback occurs, we want a detailed trace in the report (time, requests affected, latency delta).

Next steps:
1) Redwood to share the final rdw_autoscale_plan_v2.xlsx and the JMeter artifact (Aditya).
2) PayLane to provide sanitized promptset and confirm OAuth token for staging endpoints (Carlos).
3) Redwood to run synthetic baseline + burst test in the scheduled window and share raw logs + summarized SLO readout within 24h.

Appreciate the responsiveness — look forward to the test results.

Best,
Elena
Sr. SRE, PayLane
